html:
In July and August 2024 a student protest in Bangladesh grew into an uprising that ended the fifteen-year rule of Sheikh Hasina.

It began over government jobs. In June a court brought back a rule keeping 30 per cent of them for the families of those who fought in the war of 1971. Students, facing high graduate unemployment, saw it as a reward for supporters of the ruling party. They blocked roads from 1 July.

In the middle of July the ruling party's student wing and the police attacked the marches. On 16 July a student, Abu Sayed, was shot as he stood with his arms spread before a police line; the film was seen everywhere. The government shut down the internet, declared a curfew and sent in the army. Hundreds were killed. The Supreme Court cut the quota to 5 per cent, but the protesters now had one demand: that she resign.

On 5 August crowds marched on Dhaka. The army would not fire on them. Hasina left by helicopter for India, and people poured into her residence. A United Nations inquiry later put the dead at up to 1,400.

Three days later Muhammad Yunus, the founder of the Grameen Bank, was sworn in to lead a temporary government.
sum: In July and August 2024 a student protest in Bangladesh grew into an uprising that ended the fifteen-year rule of Sheikh Hasina.
